text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed on /v1/generate across multiple regions. Paging oncall. Tags: gateway, batching, scheduler, customer-impact :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: acked. I'm on it, joining. Any customer reports yet?

kevin_sre: seeing spike in 502/504 from gateway LB -> inference-proxy. Error rate up from ~0.2% to ~9% in last 6m. Latency tail rising, qps steady. Looks like backend queue backlog causing timeouts.

maya_runtime: noting a big tail in batcher queue lengths on the scheduler pods. KV cache hits normal. Recent canary deploy rolled out ~18m ago (runtime v2.13.1).

jamie_prod: getting customer DMs. A handful of mid-size customers reporting timeouts and partial responses. Not full downtime but degraded UX.

alice_oncall: immediate plan: 1) disable aggressive batching to reduce head-of-line blocking (lower batch window) 2) enable fallback routing to compat model variant (smaller model) 3) add backpressure (temporary rate limit) for large concurrent clients. Will coordinate.

kevin_sre: quick debug log snippet from scheduler pod-5:
```
[t=2026-03-14T07:12:01Z] batcher_queue_len=234 backlog_ms=4321 inflight_batches=8 head_wait=3870ms
[t=2026-03-14T07:12:03Z] enqueue_latency=120ms dequeue_latency=2100ms op=send_to_worker err=timeout
```
This matches HOL blocking where a large request holds the batch for long and others time out.

maya_runtime: I'm going to reduce max batch wait from 120ms -> 30ms and lower max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 on the scheduler config for the next few minutes. Applying to canary first.

deploy-bot: rolling config change started: runtime-scheduler/canary -> config.batch_wait_ms=30, config.max_batch_size=24.

sasha_support: pls post a short customer-facing blurb I can send to PD for proactive outreach.

alice_oncall: posting blurb in #support-ops after we have mitigation confirmed. For now we need to confirm mitigations reduce 5xx.

kevin_sre: I can also route a portion of traffic away from overloaded nodes — adding a temporary route policy to prefer warm nodes with lower queue depth. Applying now.

maya_runtime: canary change applied and telemetry shows queue lengths dropping ~60% after 90s on canary. Success signal for this config. Starting gradual push to primary pool with 20% increments.

jamie_prod: customer-impact snapshot from support: ~12 customers with intermittent timeouts, highest impact on batch endpoints (streaming generation). No data exfiltration, just errors/timeouts.

alice_oncall: good. Mitigation checklist: - propagate config to primaries - add fallback model route for large inputs - add temporary 429 for >5 concurrent requests per API key to protect shared capacity - keep deploy canary paused (do not roll new runtime code)

kevin_sre: added fallback route: requests exceeding 5s backend processing now route to model-compat-small (quantized) with best-effort output. Implemented as automated proxy fallback, will track degradation delta.

maya_runtime: rolling config to rest of scheduler pool now. Expecting full roll in ~4m.

alice_oncall: also enabling a targeted rate-limit for heavy API keys (top 1% by median tokens) to reduce HOL chances. This is temporary and will be revoked in 1h.

deploy-bot: config rollout to scheduler pool: 3/3 batches complete. No errors in rollout.

kevin_sre: metrics update: 5xx down from 9% -> 1.1% over the last 6m after full rollout. Timeouts (504) also falling. Latency p95 improved but still elevated vs baseline.

jamie_prod: passing initial update to customers. Asking for ETA to full resolution so we can update SLAs.

alice_oncall: ETA: monitoring for stable 0.5% 5xx for 15m, then we can call partially mitigated. Full resolution depends on whether we need permanent config changes or revert canary if root cause is code.

maya_runtime: digging into why HOL started — initial hypothesis: a subset of requests had very long generation lengths (tokens) that lengthened batch hold times and triggered downstream worker stalls. We're investigating traces.

kevin_sre: retrieving recent deploy history: no runtime code deploys in last 2h except the config canary which we already deployed. No infra changes.

alice_oncall: action items assigned: maya_runtime (investigate traces + root cause), kevin_sre (monitor and keep routing fallback), jamie_prod (customer comms), sasha_support (triage incoming tickets). I'll stay on until stable then hand off.

maya_runtime: found 3 anomalous requests from a single API key with very large prompt sizes (~120k tokens) hitting streaming generation. That explains the HOL. Those requests bypassed our request-size guard due to a recent parser change in gateway. Filing immediate bug.

kevin_sre: can we block that API key temporarily? If it's abuser/bug then blocking is quickest fix.

jamie_prod: support says it's probably a sandbox customer doing large synthetic tests. We can rate-limit or block after confirming.

alice_oncall: temporarily throttled that API key to 1 rps and pinned its routing to small-model fallback. Observed instant drop in batcher head wait for nodes handling that key.

sasha_support: notifying customer of throttling and asking for confirmation.

maya_runtime: root cause: gateway parser regression allowed huge token counts to surface. Patch created to re-enforce token cap on gateway parsing logic. Patch ready for deploy to canary.

alice_oncall: do not deploy runtime changes yet. Gateway fix can be deployed ASAP — that would prevent recurrence. Maya please coordinate with deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: creating canary deploy: gateway/patch/2026-03-14-01.

maya_runtime: gateway canary live. Telemetry shows new parser rejecting >50k token requests. No regressions. Rolling to primaries now.

kevin_sre: continued monitoring — 5xx down to 0.3%, p95 latencies approaching baseline. Good.

alice_oncall: turning off temporary rate-limits and fallback after 20m stable window. Rolling back API-key throttle for that customer after support confirmation.

sasha_support: customer replied, they were running a fuzz test accidentally. They understand throttling and will adjust.

jamie_prod: preparing incident summary for customers impacted. Will include timeline and remediation steps.

alice_oncall: oncall handoff plan: I'll stay for 30m to ensure stability then hand to kevin for followup/root-cause until tomorrow morning. If anything flares up before then, page me.

ops_pg: adding incident tag in tracking system and capturing key artifacts: logs, traces, config diffs.

alice_oncall: declaring incident mitigated at 1814060200 — primary mitigation: reduced batching wait and size + gateway parser fix + targeted API-key throttle + fallback routing. Customer impact limited to intermittent timeouts for ~25 minutes; ~12 customers affected, no data loss.

kevin_sre: acked handoff. I'll run deeper postmortem with maya and ops, and propose permanent guard rails: stricter gateway parsing limits, token accounting at LB, and a rate-limiter for extreme requests.

maya_runtime: agreed. I'll add a unit test in gateway to prevent this regression.

jamie_prod: thanks all. I'll craft the customer postmortem and share in #incidents-postmortems. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident Mitigated — severity: P2, duration: ~40m, runbook: scheduler-batching-hol. Postmortem owner: maya_runtime.
